[b][i]Review: [/i][/b]
After [b]700+ hours [/b] in Garry’s Mod, I can confidently say it’s not just a game—it’s [i]a recipe for disaster in the best way possible.[/i] One moment, you’re carefully building your dream rocket. The next, your friend slaps thrusters on your chair, and suddenly you’re flying across the map, screaming while everything explodes.

[b][i]Here’s what GMod taught me: [/i][/b]

1. [b]Physics don’t care about your plans.[/b] Build a masterpiece, and it’ll crumble the second you try to move it.

2. [b]Prop Hunt[/b] is just hide-and-seek for trolls. [i]Yes, that vending machine is laughing at you.[/i]

3. [b]The Workshop[/b] is a rabbit hole. You’ll go in for maps and come out with Shrek mods, flying toilets, and 1,000 unnecessary sound effects.

[b][i]Gameplay: [/i][/b]
GMod is what happens when you give players [b]unlimited freedom[/b] and [b]zero rules.[/b] Whether you’re blowing up contraptions in Build Mode, lying your way to survival in Trouble in Terrorist Town, or roleplaying as a criminal in DarkRP, it’s [i]pure chaos—and pure fun.[/i]

[b][i]Graphics and Sound: [/i][/b]
The visuals may be [b]simple,[/b] but the comedy isn’t. Whether it’s a prop hitting someone in the face or a modded sound effect that sends everyone into hysterics, it’s [i]perfect for creating unforgettable moments.[/i]

[b][i]Community: [/i][/b]
You’ll meet [b]brilliant creators, chaotic pranksters,[/b] and everyone in between. Some servers feel like art; others are just people attaching rockets to chairs and screaming. Either way, you’ll [i]laugh until your sides hurt.[/i]

I remember the first time I played Garry’s Mod.
It was late 2008. I was fifteen, my soul hungry for freedom, my heart still unaware of the weight nostalgia would one day carry.
That day, my father gave me a small gift.
A Steam card. A simple code, for my old, clunky PC.
But it wasn’t just a game.
It was the beginning of something.
It was Garry’s Mod.

I installed it, launched it, and it was as if the real world faded away.
I spent every hour of that day lost in endless possibilities.
Empty maps, bizarre contraptions, ragdolls flying through the sky — a playground where the only limit was imagination.
I wasn’t playing it. I was creating it.

And then came so many strange builds. So many weird experiments. Endless hours building cities, breaking physics, laughing at the chaos.
I knew every tool, every map, every trick with the physics gun.
And without any guide—when tutorials were rare and forums were slow—I figured out every hidden thing, every small glitch to push things further.
It was my world.
It was home.

Every now and then, my father would sit beside me.
He’d watch the screen in amusement, trying to understand what kind of “game” this even was.
He came from an era of fixed rules and high scores, so to him, this was like seeing imagination itself on the screen.
I still remember the one time I handed him the mouse and asked him to spawn a car.
He spawned twenty. All at once. And we laughed until the game crashed.
He wasn’t made for this world, but he loved seeing me inside it.
It was my refuge.
It was our small bridge.

And now, years later, I go back.
The world has changed. I have changed. I’m thirty-one now.
And he... he’s no longer here.

Yet every time I boot up Garry’s Mod, it feels like opening a window into the past.
The graphics are clunky now, the physics engine shows its age, but the heart remains untouched.
Every clang of metal, every elastic bounce, every broken object speaks a language only the soul can hear.
It’s the voice of youth.
It’s the whisper of my father laughing as the entire map collapsed under the weight of too many props.

Garry’s Mod isn’t just a game.
It’s a time machine.
It’s a second chance to touch, even for a moment, what we thought we had lost.

And as the flatgrass stretches out beneath an endless blue sky, I remain there.
Mouse in hand...
And a tear I cannot tell—whether it’s sorrow or gratitude.

Man where do I begin? 

Garrys mod has impacted my life by so much, either it be RP servers or sandbox shenanigans, those memories were priceless, such a shame most well known rp servers are being lost to time.

But in the end, I’ll never forget you.

This game got me into PC gaming. I was around 10 years old when I saw people on youtube like Venturiantale and later VanossGaming play this. I watched people play this game for 2 years until finally I got my own laptop and after a while of figuring out how to install steam (and getting a virus in the process) I bought Garry's Mod
with a steam gift card I had asked for that Christmas. My dream had come true. I played sandbox, multiplayer servers, installed a couple mods, etc. 
    I was hooked for a couple months, sinking hours into the dumb shit you could do in this game. Every video game I had ever played up to this point had no freedom compared to this game. I would think about all the things I'd do in this game when I got home from school, then spend hours finding something else to do in it, falling into a rabbit hole of creativity in the process. 
    Slowly over time the feeling died down a bit. Like most source games, this game acted as a gateway into other games on steam. I installed TF2 because of Garry's Mod, and although I wouldn't seriously play tf2 for years after installing it, it became my most played video game of all time. I've been living in a cycle with this game for over 7 years. I'd be completely obsessed with Gmod for a month then for a couple months I'd rarely play. Then I'd be driven back to this game. Back to 500+ mods and no objective.
   In my mind, this quality gives this game immortality. The sandbox which relies on people to keep building it further, unhindered by developer updates making mods obsolete or any expectation that the game has for you. This game changes constantly through modding, and the life and death of individual multiplayer servers and gamemodes, but it will never truly change. It wants nothing from you when you boot up the game. It has no qualms about your choices. 
    There is beauty in a game never changing. So many modern developers and customers want video games to be new and exciting, to such a degree that it becomes absolutely obnoxious. Such is the case with battlepasses and open beta titles which start out great then become so much better through constant fucking updates that nobody even recognizes the title anymore and they refuse to play the game. 
    Garry's Mod will never change though, it will always be the same experience you had when you played the game 7 years ago. It won't let you down because its different than it was, it expects nothing of you when you return. The only thing that does change the experience is completely optional through the workshop.
    I'm very happy to see Garry's Mod getting updates and bug fixes after all these years. It truly warms my heart that undoubtedly the greatest sandbox video game ever made is still being looked after. Just don't change the identity of this game or the innate experience of total freedom that this game provides. 

TLDR

If you want a brilliant sandbox which will never let you down despite the state of modern gaming, buy this masterpiece.

I started playing Garry's Mod last year, and it became one of the best games I have ever played. It changed my life in a way I did not expect.

The reason I started playing it was because my dad banned me from playing Roblox because of my grades. At first, I was upset and did not know what to play. Then I downloaded Steam because I thought it might have some games that were as fun as Roblox. While looking through the store, I found Garry's Mod. I thought, "Wow, this game looks really cool!" I asked my mom if she could buy it for me, and thankfully she did.

When I first started playing, the game was a little difficult for me to understand. There were so many things to learn, and I did not know how to use all the tools. But after spending more time in the game, I started getting better and having a lot of fun. I learned how to build things, use mods, and explore different maps.

What makes Garry's Mod special is that there are almost no limits to what you can do. You can create your own adventures, build amazing things, and play with thousands of community-made addons. Every time I played, I found something new to try.

Garry's Mod changed my life because it helped me discover creativity and problem-solving. Instead of just playing a game, I was making my own fun and learning new things. Even though I started playing it because I could not play Roblox anymore, I am glad that happened because I found a game that I truly enjoy.

Overall, I would highly recommend Garry's Mod to anyone who likes creativity, freedom, and endless possibilities. It is one of the best games I have ever played, and I will never forget the memories I have made in it.

With Garry's Mod turning 20 years old soon enough, I'd like to leave a review about it, more so because at one point beautiful creations really deserve the best efforts. Garry's Mod is just that.

When I was 6, this game came out, and my brother eventually bought it for us. We had little to no cash as a family of a single mom, so when my brother and I could resonate over a game, it was a ritual to bide our time with it as much as possible. Sometimes they were bad games, sometimes they were Garry's Mod. It was and is cheap as hell, so our Mom took little convincing for once!

We loved valve games, and as bad as a child can be at games, I was a valve kid. CSS, HL2, the works. Not a second I would take back for the world mind you, because for a little kid like me, they *were* my world.

That is Garry's Mod in a nutshell. It is a collective world that a child can get lost in, playing with the pieces of so many fragments of other worlds. As someone who couldn't always afford the internet, Garry's Mod was always there. I could play on gm_flatgrass or gm_construct throwing gman around and cope over stupid stuff a kid shouldn't ever have to go through irl. The early stuff of this millennium was often like that, local, and truly yours to make your own how you would like it. I covet that freedom these days, because kids now have to really dig for it; I think its still there if you look for it.

Gmod still represents all of that to this day, and it is a beautiful silly thing. Thanks for reading!

Garry's Mod holds some of my most precious memories. It has quite a bit of variety, with every server being different from the other in many ways. There are a lot of very different gamemodes which offer very different experiences, that is the reason I have so many hours played in Gmod. However, I feel that Gmod strayed away from what it used to be after the gmod 13 update. Now there are far more possibilities for content creators, which gave the community a lot of great custom content, but it has downsides. Now players have to spend a lot of time downloading that custom content while joining almost any server. There is less gamemode variety, there are only a bunch of gamemodes that are popular nowadays. SBox, TTT, many different versions of RolePlay(most of the servers and players), ZS, and a bunch of other select classic gamemodes have a lot of servers dedicated to them, with their own dedicated communities, while some gamemodes are utterly underappreciated, I will always remember Darkest Days, in my opinion a very good gamemode with great mechanics and depth, with a lot of work put into it, but it has only 1 server, and almost no one ever plays it. 

Finding good servers can be a hassle now, they can have terrible balancing and P2W(servers that involve PvP), a bunch of useless addons that you have to spend time downloading/installing. But if you find a server you like, you can keep playing on it for quite some time, if you get tired of the gamemode, you can find a good server for a different gamemode and so on. In my opinion, gmod is well worth its price for the amount of time you can spend enjoying it, unless you can't stand unpolished games, Gmod will always feel a bit weird, its a lot better in that respect than before though.

Garry’s Mod is one of those games that becomes whatever you want it to be. I play it with my son and it has turned into a modern day sandbox where you can create almost anything you can imagine. There is no real storyline or goal. You just jump in, pick tools, grab props, and build whatever comes to mind. That is the whole magic of it.

The physics system is where the fun really starts. You can stack objects, throw things around, make machines, build cars, create scenes, or just mess around with ragdolls and see what happens. Half the fun is experimenting and watching your ideas fall apart in hilarious ways. It is simple, but that freedom is what makes the game feel endless.

The game also has a huge amount of community content. There are maps, models, game modes, and tools that other players have made, and you can download whatever you want to try out. Some are silly, some are creative, and some are full game modes on their own. It gives you more variety than most games ever offer.

Playing with my son makes it even better. We end up laughing at the weird things we build or the strange moments that happen because of the physics. It is creative in a fun way, and it encourages imagination instead of pushing you into a set path. You can build, explore, roleplay, try challenges, or just mess around for the sake of it.

The graphics are older, but the game does not need fancy visuals to be entertaining. The focus is on creativity and freedom, and it works. You just jump in and do whatever your brain decides.

Overall, Garry’s Mod is a huge open toolbox that lets you and your friends or family make your own fun. If you enjoy creative games or just want something you can experiment with together, this one is perfect.

[h1] Garrys Mod	[/h1]

The most enjoyable and mod filled game on steam, Garrys Mod. Garrys Mod is an amazing game with a good amount of gamemodes and lovely servers. You may want to play Sandbox and smack around batman or play TTT and rage because you were rdmed.

[h1] Gameplay 	[/h1]  

Garrys mod does not have a specific type of gameplay ranging from Prop Hunt to Stop It Slender. However your gameplay can be significantly improved by using the steam workshop and adding items.

[h1] Mods 	[/h1]

Garrys mod is a game focused upon the premise of random and fun addons. I personally enjoy being a watermelon and firing pizzas from a bazooka. Garrys mod has an amazing amount of mods including characters and items. This is a game focused around its modding community.

[h1] TTT (Trouble In Terrorist Town)	[/h1]

TTT is the most famous gamemode in Garrys Mod. The premise of the game is simple. At the begining you are assigned a role, you are either an innocent bystander, a detective, or a traitor. However do not worry if you are innocent for this is trouble in terrorist town meaning everybody had guns. The innocent and the detectives try to find out who the traitors are while the traitors try to kill them all off. The gamemode is fun and server usually will have cool player models or gun. The main downside with TTT is rdmer's. RDM stand for Random Death Match and an rdmer is someone who out of the blue will try to kill you. This means an inno/detective randomly kills an inno/detective or a traitor kills an traitor or an inno just randomly kills someone who is a T. This really spoil's the gamemode making it unenjoyable at times but usually admins or mods will be on to help you or they will have an option to directly report it to kick/ban the person. 

[h1] Sandbox 	[/h1]

Sandbox is where creativity and stupidity flourish. Sandbox is where you can get all your downloaded mods and just have fun. Sandbox is just fooling around and having fun. It is one of Garrys Mod most hilarious game modes (if you play with the right people).

[h1] Singleplayer/Muliplayer	[/h1]

So if your planning on playing Sandbox I would recommend playing singleplayer or creating a hamachi or another program to play with a select group of friends,

If you plan to play other gamemodes I suggest playing multiplayer and trying to find a nice server which you can enjoy.

[h1] Rating	[/h1]

[b] Pros	[/b]
+ fun alone or with friends
+ many gamemodes to enjoy
+ massive amount of creative and fun mods
+ overall great community
+ highly enjoyable 

[b] Cons	[/b]
- rdmers
- will end up overloading computer with mods

[h1] Final Thoughts	[/h1]

Garrys Mod is a must buy with its countless possibilities. It may take you a while to find a nice server or the gamemode that is for you but when you find it good times will be waiting. The mods are just so amazing that I salute all the mod makers for their effort and allowing me to become a watermelon with a portal gun.

At first, I was going to make a review about garry's mod, and why I've found it unfun recently. But then I had a revalation. A eureka moment, of sorts. At first, I joined a MilitaryRp server, waited 10 minutes to be trained, then left.

It wasn't fun.

I got bored so I decided to join and troll a dark "rp" server (heavy quotes on rp) just to laugh at all the bad servers. I joined, picked the dog job the server had, walked up behind someone, and said as loudly as I could "OMAE WA MO SHINDERU" and started attacking him. This turned into 10 minutes of role-playing as a edgy anime character, ending with a final duel between me and the guy I tried to kill. He pulled out his ultimate werewolf form and defeated me.


It was fun.

This is what made me realize what garry's mod is, and why it's fun. Garry's mod isn't really a serious game. It's not meant to be taken seriously. I mean, look at the store pictures for it. Doesn't it just shout "serious military roleplay"? When you take garry's mod, and try to bring seriousness to it, it's hard. Take the MilitaryRp server, for example. Why did I even need to be trained? I've played those servers before, and they ALL make you go through training. All they teach you are meaningless boring stuff, like ranks, faces, and other things that you probably never use.

When you try to make this game a slog of rules, it just ruins it. 

This game shines when silly stuff happens, and is encouraged. You can do some weird stuff too.

Try it.

See what weird stuff you can come up with.

Never be serious.

A Spiritual Journey Through GMOD

Oh, Garry’s Mod. Truly, a masterpiece of the modern gaming world. There’s nothing quite like the feeling of waking up, launching the game, and immediately discovering that half your mods are now completely broken because of some update that no one asked for. It’s like a beautiful sunrise, if the sunrise were a slap to the face.

In this utopia of user-created content, we wander the barren landscape of abandoned mods like forlorn nomads, desperately clinging to the hope that—just maybe—some forgotten modder will descend from the heavens to patch that one line of code that makes everything work again. Spoiler alert: It’s not happening. They're not coming back. The great modders have ascended to their higher calling—probably making money in the real world, leaving us here to weep over broken content and incomplete files. RIP, sweet mods. You were too pure for this world.

And to all the brave souls considering entering this kingdom of digital despair: Please, for the love of whatever's left of your sanity—don’t. Don’t you dare play this game. Every new player is a harbinger of doom, bringing with them updates that will crush the few remaining mods we have left. You want to be a hero? Then stay away. Don’t download Garry’s Mod. Let it live in its broken, unfinished glory. Let it die peacefully without the constant interruption of progress.

Because, let’s face it: every update is a reminder that the modding community has long since moved on. We're stuck here, trying to convince ourselves that somehow, somehow, the mods we love will magically work again if we just tweak a few files and pray to the modding gods. It’s a sick joke. And we’re all in on it.

And yet, here I am, trudging through this endless cycle, faithfully playing Garry’s Mod in its gloriously broken state until my dying breath.
